solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irish clan established around Priesthaggard originally

indicators.note: to sit around something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: something established is set, as in set up or fixed

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the invented place name

explanation.surface: A family clan setting up home near an Irish-sounding village called Priesthaggard.
explanation.walkthrough: Priesthaggard is not a real place to look up; it exists only to supply its first letter, which sits inside SET to give SEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a branch or subdivision of a family, used especially of the old Irish and Scottish clan system.

clue.text: Sultan's palace complex is large and old

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A description of a sultan's palace complex as being big and ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as a noun next to 'palace', as in a palace complex, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the walled women's quarters or palace of a Turkish sultan, the Topkapi in Istanbul being the famous example.

clue.text: Joke I'd set up and attempt, expressing expert opinion

definitions.note: a gerund phrase standing for the noun, the activity itself

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so its letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the contraction written without its apostrophe
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: A comedian rigging a gag and then having a go, while sounding off like an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I'd is turned round; the joke and the attempt sit either side in their normal order.
explanation.definitionFit: Punditry is the giving of opinions by pundits, the experts called on by television and newspapers to comment.

clue.text: Landlord initially thrown by elusive girl's rental arrangement

indicators.note: a rider thrown by a horse is ejected from it, so one letter is cast out of the word

parts.note: something elusive is subtle, hard to pin down

indicators.note: what comes initially comes first, so only the opening letter is meant

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a girl's name; the 's joins it to what follows

explanation.surface: A landlord is thrown off balance by a slippery young woman's arrangement for renting a property.
explanation.walkthrough: The landlord looks like a character in the story, but he only supplies one letter, and 'thrown by' means that letter is ejected rather than that he is confused.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtenancy is the letting of a property by an existing tenant to someone else, a sublet being one kind of rental arrangement.

clue.text: Old soldier's high-class article about hard left

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so the outer letters wrap the inner

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class speech and manners
the indefinite article
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier writes a posh newspaper piece about the hard left of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: U and AN together form the outer shell, with H and L placed between them. 'Hard left' reads as a political phrase but is just two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An uhlan was a lancer in the cavalry of several European armies, notably the Polish and Prussian, now a historical type of soldier.

clue.text: Body artist first to support military pageant

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever supports something holds it up from below, so it comes after

parts.note: a tattoo is a military display of marching and music, like the Edinburgh one
1st, with the digit 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: An artist who paints bodies is the first to back a military parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body artist first' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'artist'. Crosswords often write the digit 1 as I, so 1st becomes IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist decorates people's skin with permanent designs, so the human body is the canvas this artist works on.

clue.text: Miners rational about famous statue, endlessly studying figures

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go around the statue's letters

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union
logical means rational

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the statue's name

parts.note: Eros is the famous statue at Piccadilly Circus in London

explanation.surface: Miners being sensible about a famous statue while busy with numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: NUM (the miners' union) and LOGICAL go 'about' ERO, which is EROS (the Piccadilly Circus statue in London) 'endlessly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerological work studies the supposed mystical significance of numbers, which are figures.

clue.text: Scandinavian chap raised one in the Washington area

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a man's name standing for any chap

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: the District of Columbia, the area covered by the city of Washington
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian man grew up as the only one of his kind around Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests bringing up a child, but it turns the name round; the I then goes inside DC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic is the adjective for the peoples and countries of northern Europe, including Scandinavia, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Cowardly to react thus to being hurt?

parts.note: to yell is to react by shouting
the cry anyone makes on being hurt; 'thus' says what is shouted

explanation.surface: A question whether reacting this way to pain shows a lack of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a little scene: you yell the cry of pain. The reader must supply the word for the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is an informal word for timid, from the old association of that colour with a lack of courage.

clue.text: Frenchman introducing canon backing restoration

indicators.note: whoever introduces someone comes first and presents them, so this piece leads

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: something backing goes backwards, so its letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a canon is a law or rule, especially of the church

explanation.surface: A Frenchman brings in a churchman who supports the restoration of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests a cathedral clergyman, which fits the restoration story, but here it means a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is the act of making something new or fresh again, which is what a restoration also does.

clue.text: Musical politician overwhelmed by bridge-player's tragic day

indicators.note: in a down clue, a thing overwhelmed by others lies beneath them, so it comes last

parts.note: West is one of the four seats at a bridge table; the 's adds an S
the Ides of March, the day Julius Caesar was assassinated
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician is crushed by a card player's disastrous day, set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: The breaks between the pieces fall in different places from the breaks in the title. In bridge the players are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: West Side Story is the Bernstein and Sondheim stage show retelling Romeo and Juliet among New York gangs.

clue.text: Wood turns tail, having left instrument in the kitchen

indicators.note: turns tail means only the last pair of letters of the wood word is flipped round

parts.note: timber is wood

explanation.surface: A wooden thing flips over and leaves an instrument behind in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the kitchen' is orchestral slang for the percussion section, which makes the definition fair; 'turns tail' acts on just the end of the wood word.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbrel is a tambourine-like hand drum, a percussion instrument, played in the orchestra's percussion section.

clue.text: Broadcast losing sad musical slide

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio programme drops a melancholy song about sliding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a noun or a verb about radio, and 'losing' like a deletion signal, but both of the last two words are the letters to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through a series of notes, as when a pianist sweeps a finger along the keys.

clue.text: Character in Thessaloniki carrying home money

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and Thessaloniki is a Greek city
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone in a Greek city takes cash back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it means a letter of the alphabet; the city tells you which alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for cash, recorded since the seventeenth century, so it is a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Enticing berries I still mostly supply

indicators.note: supply read as supplely, in a pliant way, tells us the letters bend into a new order
mostly drops the last letter of still

explanation.surface: Tempting berries that I still mostly provide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' (read as 'in a supple way') rearranges BERRIES, I and STIL ('still' 'mostly').
explanation.definitionFit: Something irresistible is too tempting to refuse, so it is enticing.

clue.text: Most of deprived area in resort, one serving Italian food

indicators.note: in puts the shortened area inside the resort and one together

parts.note: a spa is a resort town
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: Most of drops the last letter

parts.note: a ghetto is a deprived area

explanation.surface: Someone in a resort, from a poor district, serves Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts GHETTO short, and it goes 'in' SPA plus I; 'one serving' looks like a waiter, but one is just I and 'serving' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, a staple dish of Italian cuisine.

clue.text: A lot of skill required to capture neat craft?

definitions.note: the question mark flags the less common sense, cunning rather than skill or a boat

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold inside, so one piece goes within the other
a lot of something stops short of all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: finesse is delicate skill
neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one

explanation.surface: Building a tidy little boat takes great skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but crosswords use it in its old sense of cattle. 'Craft' then means cunning, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxiness is slyness or cunning, like that of the fox in fables, and craft is likewise a word for wily cunning.

clue.text: A second US statesman perhaps, not a political enabler

indicators.note: 'not' says the next word is excluded, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for second
a member of the US Senate, given as an example by 'perhaps'
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A deputy American politician, maybe, who refuses to back someone's campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' looks like a negation of the definition, but it is the instruction to remove one A from SENATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In British elections an assentor is one of the voters who sign a candidate's nomination paper, so enabling the candidacy.

clue.text: Useful publicity label on vehicle taking MDMA round the States

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is added after it

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
a van is a vehicle
a tag is a label
E is slang for ecstasy, the drug MDMA
the letter O is round
the United States

explanation.surface: Promotional stickers on a van carrying drugs around America prove handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like it puts one piece around another, but it simply gives O in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advantageous gives an advantage or benefit, so it is helpful in the same way as anything useful.

clue.text: Old woman's ultimately serious condition, a rocky situation

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old woman in slang, with the 's

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes at the very end, so the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A mother's grave illness turns out to be a difficult, stony time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rocky situation' sounds like a crisis, but it is a literal pile of rock. 'Old woman' is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a great mass of rock occupying one place in the landscape.

clue.text: Asian dish having edge over a French fricassee initially

indicators.note: something turned over is upside down, so in a down clue the letters read upward

parts.note: a lip is the edge of a cup or jug
taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for French

indicators.note: what comes initially comes first, so only the opening letter is meant

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Eastern rice dish claims an advantage over a French stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having edge over' reads as being better than, but 'edge' is LIP and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is a rice dish cooked in stock with spices, found from Turkey through Iran to India.

clue.text: Idiot crossing motorway? That's out of order

indicators.note: to cross something here is to span it, so one piece stretches around another

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the M1, the London to Leeds motorway, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A fool dodging traffic on a motorway gets told off for unacceptable behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first and best-known motorway, and crosswords write its 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is wrong or not as it should be, just as something out of order is faulty or improper.

clue.text: Holy Willie, type involved with choir

indicators.note: something involved is tangled and complicated, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pious man named Willie is the sort who gets mixed up with the church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Holy Willie is the sanctimonious churchman of Robert Burns's satirical poem Holy Willie's Prayer, a byword for false piety.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns's Holy Willie condemns others' sins while excusing his own, the very model of a person who fakes virtue.

clue.text: Advance after crossing island

definitions.note: the verb, to put forward an idea

indicators.note: to cross something here is to span it, so one piece stretches around another

parts.note: post- is the prefix meaning after
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone moves forward having crossed an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' reads as moving forward, but the sense needed is putting forward an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition for argument, the same as advancing a theory or claim.

clue.text: European in South Africa left Durban for example

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
E is the standard abbreviation for European
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A European in South Africa departed from Durban, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed, fitting the travel story, but it is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban, on the Indian Ocean coast of KwaZulu-Natal, is one of Africa's busiest harbours, an example of a coastal town for shipping.

clue.text: Conspicuous way to accommodate a legal right

indicators.note: to accommodate means the street takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: An eye-catching street holds a legal entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: ST (way) 'accommodates' A plus LIEN, a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means most noticeable or prominent, hence standing out conspicuously.

clue.text: What's shown by a couple of Liberals briefly sharing equally?

parts.words: What's shown by a couple of Liberals briefly
parts.note: surface reading: what two members of the Liberal party might display; setter's reading: two Liberals abbreviated are LL, and each L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A question about how two Liberal politicians would divide things evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to write the two abbreviated Liberals down as LL and then read each L as a Roman numeral, spelling out its value in words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty-fifty describes a split into two halves of equal size, so both parties get the same amount.

clue.text: In Massachusetts, a respected national leader once

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters are found inside the words that follow, running across the gap

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the state name, the article and the start of the adjective

explanation.surface: A well-regarded former national leader comes from the state of Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma between the state and the article must be ignored for the letters to join up.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the emperor of Russia until the 1917 revolution, so the title belongs to a national ruler of the past.
